KC-E1's primary was met on both legs -- PERSON entity WER 22.489 -> 18.341, +4.148 pp with a call-clustered CI90 lower bound of +2.633 -- and the cell was still REJECTED, because the brief bought 152 PERSON substitutions with 2,242 extra non-entity deletions and both the corpus-WER and numeric guards failed. The one factor here is therefore the CONSUMPTION FORM, not the knowledge: pass 1 is not re-flown (the sealed comparator supplies each window's hypothesis through a content-free snapshot binding), pass 2 sees the window's audio, that hypothesis and the same cap-12 brief, and a registered response post-processor admits SUBSTITUTIONS only -- so the deletion profile is the comparator's by construction and the guard KC-E1 failed cannot be failed the same way.

predecessor.why_it_is_not_reflown: the comparator already decoded every one of these windows, and its bytes ARE pass 1. Re-flying pass 1 would double the contacts, spend a second pass of GPU hours, and -- because greedy decoding on llama-server is not bitwise reproducible across batch compositions -- would produce a pass 1 that is NOT the arm this cell is paired against. Binding the sealed one makes the comparison exact and the cell cost one contact per window.
predecessor.what_the_binding_commits: a content-free receipt: the artifact's path, size and sha256, the sealed manifest/outputs/trace hashes, the counts, and a chain hash over (window_id, text_sha256). The per-window hypotheses are model output and live under SPEECHRL_DATA_DIR with the sealed outputs, never in Git.

comparator.why_it_is_also_the_equal_contact_control: the comparator sends ONE contact per window and no pass-2 contact at all; KC-E1f sends one pass-2 contact per window over the comparator's own delivered text. The pair therefore isolates the pass-2 contact plus the brief, and the twin below isolates the brief's content net of that contact.
comparator.pairing_rule: docs/readiness/2026-09-06-earnings-agentic-metric-baseline-v1.md section 7 and the KC-E1 verdict's own instrument: the fixed 90-second window is the paired unit (1,593), the call is the bootstrap cluster (44), the estimator is the pooled ratio through analysis.paired.resampled_statistic with cluster_of=analysis.e21_window_pairing.call_of, seed 20260903, 10,000 replicates, CI90.

one_factor.between_the_two_cells: the brief's CONTENT. The two baseline fragments differ in exactly two keys, evidence_source and the twin's own pad-plan byte pin; the policy, the arm, the predecessor binding, the repair frame, the response post-processor and its parameters, the task instruction, the scorers, the OBS protocol, the cap and every decoding parameter are byte-identical.
one_factor.against_the_sealed_comparator: TWO things move and this document says so rather than hiding it: a second contact per window exists at all, and that contact carries the brief plus a repair instruction. The comparator contrast is therefore reported as repair-pass-plus-brief; the CONTENT attribution comes from the twin, which pays the identical contact.
one_factor.against_kc_e1: the consumption FORM, at identical knowledge. KC-E1 and KC-E1f supply the same cap-12 brief built from the same two ConEC files by the same transform; they differ in whether the brief conditions the only decode or edits a sealed one. That contrast is reported as a cross-cell reading, never as this cell's decision.

shared_protocol.prompt_order: evidence-first-system-v3 (from the model fragment): the evidence blocks precede the audio, and the pass-1 hypothesis rides at the END of the rendered task_instruction inside the frozen frame e21-entity-repair-frame-v1 -- exactly where reproduction.obs_loop's own OBS_TAIL_FRAME_V1 conditioned tail rides. It is model output, framed as model output, never a reference transcript, and it lands verbatim in the sealed MODEL_REQUEST record.
shared_protocol.contacts_per_item: ONE per 90-second window; 1,593 windows over 44 calls per cell. Pass 1 is read, not flown.
shared_protocol.delivery_rule: core.base.RESPONSE_POSTPROCESSORS entry e21-entity-repair-substitutions-v1 (core.repair_alignment): whitespace-token alignment against the sealed pass-1 hypothesis, accepting a replace only when both sides carry the same token count and that count is <= 4; insertions, deletions and unbalanced or oversized replaces are rejected without changing a byte; an empty response, an anchor ratio below 0.60 or accepted substitutions covering more than 10 % of the pass-1 tokens refuse the whole response and deliver pass 1 verbatim. The delivered token count equals the predecessor's on every window, asserted in code.
shared_protocol.harness: core.driver.run_experiment_bundled through the same committed launcher path the comparator and KC-E1 flew; the registered core.base policy obs-repair-loop is ObsAgentLoopPolicy with ONE method overridden.

evaluation.paper_facing_metric: ConEC-mirror entity WER per entity type, PERSON first; corpus WER stays the anchor and the harm check
mandatory_slices: per entity class, with reference-word counts, beside ConEC Table 2 rows 1 / 5 / 8 and beside KC-E1's own per-class table
all 44, the construction 34 and the evaluation 10, reported apart
the repair ledger: windows refused by reason, windows changed, accepted substitutions, substituted tokens, and rejected opcodes by class -- all four classes reported even at zero

the delivered-vs-comparator operation table: substitutions, deletions and insertions against the comparator's 13,098 / 5,701 / 10,700. The delivery is substitution-only in RAW whitespace-token space by construction; the Whisper normalizer is not a per-token map, so a substituted surface form may normalize to a different number of words and the normalized deletion/insertion counts can move by that delta alone. Every such move is reported with the substitution that caused it, and a move that cannot be attributed to a substituted span is a defect report, not a result (preregistration section 5.1)
